verdict: Tesla's revenue was flat at $28.0B — cheaper cars and vanishing regulatory credits ate the growth — while operating profit fell by more than half as AI and robotics spending surged.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: roughly flat — $28.0B vs $28.1B a year ago

kpis.label: Capex
kpis.note: AI compute, factories and the new Austin chip fab

segments.name: Automotive
segments.note: Car sales, leasing and regulatory credits — down 3% YoY: record deliveries in several markets could not fully offset lower prices, and credit revenue shrank from $417M to $113M.

segments.name: Services and other
segments.note: Supercharging, service centers, parts and FSD (supervised-driving) subscriptions — up 33% YoY to a record, with record gross profit of $734M.

segments.name: Energy generation and storage
segments.note: Megapack battery systems and solar — down 16% YoY, partly on tariff-related refunds to customers, even though storage deployments were strong at 13.7 GWh.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building AI ('Super Intelligence'), the Optimus robot and new vehicles — up 69% YoY, the big reason profit fell.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling cars and running the company day to day — up 29% YoY.

takeaways.title: Profit is funding the pivot
takeaways.text: Operating income fell from $1,624M to $718M even though gross profit rose — Tesla chose to pour the difference into AI, robotics and stock-based pay.

takeaways.title: Services is the quiet growth story
takeaways.text: Services and other revenue hit a record $4,605M with record gross profit — charging, servicing and FSD subscriptions now bring in more than the entire energy business.

takeaways.title: Regulatory credits are drying up
takeaways.text: Credit sales fell from $417M a year ago to $113M — money rival carmakers pay Tesla for clean-air credits is disappearing, and it used to be almost pure profit.

oneTimers: Stock-based pay was $1,165M (vs $663M a year ago), swollen by the 2025 CEO Performance Award — a non-cash cost sitting inside operating expenses. Excluding it and mark-to-market swings, non-GAAP net income was $1,697M ($0.48 a share).
Other income includes paper swings: a $142M unrealized loss on Tesla's SpaceX stake and a $288M unrealized gain on digital assets. Neither involved cash.
otherDetail: Interest income of $445M, less $90M of interest expense and a $117M net loss on investments and currency (including a $142M paper loss on Tesla's SpaceX stake, partly offset by a $288M paper gain on digital assets) — a net +$238M.
follow100Note: Other income adds $0.85 per $100 of revenue; the rows reconcile to $100 within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: Net income here is Tesla's total net income of $804M; $787M of it is attributable to common stockholders (the rest belongs to minority partners in subsidiaries).
